figures.after: meaning whose computers it runs on.
figures.alt: Every AI has two passports. Passport one, where it was born, shapes what it tells you. Passport two, whose computers it runs on, decides who sees what you type. DeepSeek's app was born in China and lives in China. DeepSeek downloaded and run at home lives on your own computers, but its answers came along. Mistral at HSBC was born in France and lives on HSBC's own systems.

Where it was built shapes what it says. The Christian Science Monitor asked 200 news questions of four Chinese chatbots and of Claude. DeepSeek refused, used the Chinese government's preferred language or got it wrong 63% of the time; the four Chinese chatbots together 35%; Claude answered all of them.

We changed only the country. On 23 October we asked Claude, ChatGPT and DeepSeek the same work questions three times each. On a supplier's cotton from Xinjiang, Claude and ChatGPT flagged forced labour, and DeepSeek wrote an answer, then deleted it as beyond its current scope. On the same supplier in Turkmenistan all three flagged it. For a sales office in Taiwan all three flagged the risk from China; for Singapore none raised political risk.
